subject: Renewal options: staggered term alignment + credit-bridging proposal
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightleaf.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@brightleaf.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: capacity phasing and invoicing questions

Hi Priyom / Lauren,

Thanks again for the QBR review last week. We reviewed usage and want to discuss options for the upcoming renewal. Brightleaf expects a ~2x platform spike in Y2 driven by a new personalization initiative; we also want cleaner invoice alignment with our fiscal year.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood support a 36-month term where Year 1 remains at our current committed capacity, Year 2 increases by 2x, and Year 3 holds that higher level?
- We prefer a staggered billing cadence: annual invoices but with the ability to allocate credits across years (i.e., bridge credits in year 1 to fund ramping in year 2).
- Any sections you need in the amendment to protect us for earlier-than-expected scale-downs (termination language / pro-rata true-ups)?

I attached a short capacity forecast (brightleaf_capacity_request.xlsx).

Can you propose 2 structured options (one prepay-heavy with deeper credits, one annualized with smaller immediate credits)? We need a finance-friendly version for our procurement team.

Best,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, Brightleaf Media
---
Attachment: brightleaf_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightleaf.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity phasing and invoicing questions

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear notes and the forecast.

Summary:
Option A (Prepay + Bridge Credit)
- 36-month term; Year 1 at current commit, Year 2 = 2x commit, Year 3 = 2x commit.
- Upfront prepay for Year 1 at a 7% discount + a bridge credit applied across Q1–Q4 of Year 2 to offset onboarding/scale costs.
- Invoicing: one annual invoice per year.

Option B (Annualized with staged credit)
- 36-month term; same capacity profile.
- Annual invoicing with a smaller immediate credit in Year 1 (3%) plus a usage true-up at the annual anniversary.

Trade-offs: Option A lowers unit price and helps Brightleaf with predictable spend; Option B keeps cashflow lighter but increases variability on true-ups.

I've attached a short write-up (redwood_renewal_options_v1.pdf) — Lauren, can you and Rishi validate whether we can convert the bridge credit into an invoice-level line item for accounting? If not, we should surface the alternative with an explicit prepaid bucket.

I'll consolidate numbers and share a single amendment for signature once we align.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_renewal_options_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Looping in Rishi to confirm accounting treatment. Quick thought:
- If finance can accept a line-item "Bridge Credit" that amortizes across Year 2 for revenue recognition, Option A is clean and gives Brightleaf the lower blended unit cost they want.
- If not, we should propose a "prepaid bucket" that shows on their AR and ours — same economics but simpler reconciliation for procurement.

Rishi — can you run a quick P&L sketch for both approaches (amortized credit vs prepaid bucket) and call out any revenue deferral implications we need to flag to legal? Ideally want a simple yes/no and the recommended invoice wording.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Renewal Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity phasing and invoicing questions

Thanks — did a quick pass. Key points:
- Amortized bridge credit: revenue should be recognized over the period the credit applies (Year 2). We can model this as a contra-revenue amortized monthly. That works but requires clear contract language: total credit amount, schedule of amortization, and trigger events (i.e., if Brightleaf scales slower than forecast, remaining unamortized credit is forfeited or rolled into future true-up).
- Prepaid bucket: simpler for procurement; revenue recognized as usage is consumed (deferral into deferred revenue and released against consumption). Sales ops needs a simple SKU for the prepaid bucket so finance can reconcile.

Numbers (ballpark):
- Current ARR: $1.2M
- Year 2 committed cost @2x: additional $1.2M incremental, with Option A netting a 7% effective discount = ~$2.34M over Y2 (after credits).
- If we do prepaid bucket, we need invoice language: "Prepaid Capacity Bucket — non-refundable except for Arkansas statute — applied to account usage at the agreed commit rates; unused bucket balance will be true-upped at annual anniversary." (we'll tighten legal.)

I've attached a short calc sheet (finance_summary_BRIEF.xlsx). I'm OK with either option; recommend Option A if Brightleaf signs the amortization schedule and accepts the forfeiture clause — that reduces our billing churn risk.

Rishi
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations

Samir — appreciate the fast turnaround. Based on the internal review, here is a consolidated recommendation and next step: 

Proposed (consolidated)
- 36-month term; Year 1 = current commit, Year 2 = 2x commit, Year 3 = 2x commit.
- Primary option = Option A (Prepay + Bridge Credit): 7% Year 1 prepay discount + bridge credit amortized across Year 2. We include a forfeiture clause if actual Year 2 consumption < 75% of forecasted ramp (standard protection for us).
- Backup option = Option B (Annualized): 3% immediate credit in Year 1 + annual true-up at anniversary.

Invoicing cadence: annual invoice each year. For Option A the invoice will show: Prepay amount (line item), Bridge Credit (contra line with amortization schedule noted in amendment).

Next steps: I uploaded a draft amendment and DocuSign envelope for your review: renewal_amendment_docusign_link.txt (link in attachments). If Brightleaf is happy, countersign and we will schedule a legal clean-up call for the forfeiture wording (optional).

If you want to preserve flexibility on burst capacity during Year 2, we can add a 60-day notice for any >25% temporary bump — would that work?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the DocuSign if helpful.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
